# Graphic Grammar and Core API

`cliplot()` provides a single entry point for generating biomedical visualizations through a formula syntax. This chapter details the formula grammar, the parameter system (`clipar`), and the type dispatch architecture.

## Formula Syntax

`cliplot()` accepts standard R formulas mapping variables to visual roles:

- `y ~ x`: Bivariate plots (boxplots, scatter plots, violin plots, ROC curves).
- `y ~ x | facet`: Conditioned plots faceted across biological subgroups or clinical trial cohorts.
- `Surv(time, event) ~ arm`: Time-to-event outcomes with survival curves, risk tables, and hazard ratios.
- `~ x`: Univariate distributions (histograms, density estimates, rank-abundance curves).

```r
# General syntax
p <- cliplot(
  formula = Value ~ Biomarker,
  data    = clinical_data,
  type    = "boxplot",
  preset  = "nature"
)
```

## Function Dispatch and Plot Types

The `type` argument selects the geometry and statistical layer. It accepts either character aliases or typed constructor functions:

```{r grammar-demo}
library(cliomicplot)
library(ggplot2)

# Generate reproducible clinical cohort
set.seed(42)
df_cohort <- data.frame(
  Biomarker  = factor(rep(c("Control", "Mild_AD", "Severe_AD"), each = 40),
                      levels = c("Control", "Mild_AD", "Severe_AD")),
  Treatment  = factor(rep(rep(c("Placebo", "Biologic"), each = 20), 3),
                      levels = c("Placebo", "Biologic")),
  Age_Group  = factor(rep(c("Pediatric", "Adult"), 60)),
  IL13_pg_ml = c(rnorm(40, 4.2, 1.1), rnorm(40, 8.5, 1.8), rnorm(40, 15.2, 2.9))
)

# Direct character specification
p_box <- cliplot(
  IL13_pg_ml ~ Biomarker,
  data   = df_cohort,
  type   = "boxplot",
  preset = "nature",
  title  = "Serum IL-13 by Clinical Severity"
)
p_box
```

### Typed Constructor Functions

Constructor functions configure geometry-specific options with autocomplete support:

```{r constructor-demo}
p_viol <- cliplot(
  IL13_pg_ml ~ Biomarker,
  data  = df_cohort,
  type  = type_violin(inner = "boxplot", trim = FALSE),
  theme = "lancet"
)
p_viol
```

## Distribution Architectures: Violin and Split-Violin Plots

Violin plots show probability density distributions across categorical cohorts. `cliomicplot` provides four interior anatomy modes (`inner`), two-condition split violins, and hypothesis tests.

### 1. Interior Quantile Density Lines: `inner = "quartiles"`

Drawing 25%, 50% (median), and 75% quantile lines inside the density polygon avoids visual clutter while reporting the interquartile range:

```{r violin-quantiles-demo, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=4.8}
p_quant <- cliplot(
  IL13_pg_ml ~ Biomarker,
  data    = df_cohort,
  by      = "Biomarker",
  type    = type_violin(inner = "quartiles", quantiles = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75), add_jitter = FALSE),
  palette = "nature",
  legend  = "none",
  title   = "Serum IL-13 Distribution with Interior Quartiles",
  subtitle = "Quantile lines at 25%, median, and 75% within each density contour",
  ylab    = "Serum IL-13 (pg/mL)"
)
p_quant
```

### 2. Dual-Condition Contrast: `type_split_violin()`

When evaluating two treatment arms (such as Placebo vs. Biologic) across multiple disease severity tiers, `type_split_violin()` draws the left half for group 1 and the right half for group 2 on a shared category axis:

```{r split-violin-demo, fig.width=8.0, fig.height=5.0}
p_split <- cliplot(
  IL13_pg_ml ~ Biomarker | Treatment,
  data    = df_cohort,
  type    = type_split_violin(
    inner     = "quartiles",
    quantiles = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75),
    scale     = "width"
  ),
  palette = "jco",
  title   = "IL-13 Shift Under Biologic vs. Placebo Across Severity Tiers",
  subtitle = "Split-half density comparison: Placebo (left) vs. Biologic (right)",
  ylab    = "Serum IL-13 (pg/mL)",
  xlab    = "Biomarker Severity Tier"
)
p_split
```

`type_violin(split = TRUE)` produces the same split geometry when the formula contains a two-level conditioning variable (`| group`).

### 3. Mean Diamond Glyphs and Hypothesis Testing: `inner = "mean_se"`

Setting `inner = "mean_se"` overlays a central diamond for the arithmetic mean with standard error errorbars. Adding `stat.test = "wilcox.test"` calculates the non-parametric Wilcoxon rank-sum p-value:

```{r violin-mean-stat-demo, fig.width=6.0, fig.height=4.8}
p_stat <- cliplot(
  IL13_pg_ml ~ Treatment,
  data      = df_cohort,
  by        = "Treatment",
  type      = type_violin(
    inner        = "mean_se",
    add_jitter   = TRUE,
    jitter_width = 0.12,
    jitter_alpha = 0.40,
    jitter_size  = 1.6
  ),
  palette   = "cell",
  legend    = "none",
  stat.test = "wilcox.test",
  title     = "Biologic Efficacy on Circulating IL-13",
  subtitle  = "Violin density with raw observations, mean ± SEM diamond, and Wilcoxon test",
  ylab      = "Serum IL-13 (pg/mL)"
)
p_stat
```

## The Parameter Object: `clipar()`

`clipar()` sets visual attributes including line widths, point sizes, alpha transparency, jitter jitter-width, and label font sizes:

```{r clipar-demo}
pars <- clipar(
  point_size  = 2.2,
  line_width  = 0.9,
  alpha       = 0.75,
  font_size   = 10
)

p_custom <- cliplot(
  IL13_pg_ml ~ Biomarker,
  data   = df_cohort,
  type   = "beeswarm",
  params = pars,
  preset = "science"
)
p_custom
```

## Plot Composition and Layer Addition

`cliplot()` objects are `ggplot2` instances. You can extend them using the standard `+` operator or the `cliplot_add()` helper:

```{r add-layers}
p_final <- p_box +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 10, linetype = "dashed", color = "#B22222", linewidth = 0.6) +
  annotate("text", x = 1.2, y = 10.8, label = "Diagnostic Threshold (10 pg/mL)",
           size = 2.8, color = "#B22222", fontface = "bold")
p_final
```
